plays.story: A leak claims D&D's next major crossover product is a World of Warcraft tie-in, breaking right alongside a livestream podcast dissecting the leak

angles.bizzal-games: Title: 'Is a D&D x World of Warcraft Sourcebook Really Coming? Here's What GMs Should Start Prepping For' — break down the leak's crunch: new classes/races, adventure hooks, and whether tables should hold off on homebrew Azeroth conversions until WotC confirms.
angles.itsalreadywritten: Title: 'The Alliance and Horde Roll Initiative: What a WoW–D&D Crossover Means for Shared-World Canon' — take the narrative/lore angle on merging two decades-deep fictional universes into one ruleset, and what gets lost or gained when Azeroth's story bends to d20 mechanics.

plays.story: Paizo and Archives of Nethys formalize their relationship, securing the future of the most-used free Pathfinder/Starfinder rules database

angles.bizzal-games: Title: 'Paizo Just Locked In Your Favorite Free Pathfinder Database — Here's What Actually Changes for GMs' — practical breakdown of what the new agreement means for access, updates, and whether third-party tools built on Nethys are safe long-term.
angles.itsalreadywritten: Title: 'How a Fan-Run Wiki Became Pathfinder's De Facto Canon — and Why Paizo Just Made It Official' — the lore-preservation angle: when community documentation becomes the accepted record of a game's fiction, formalizing it is basically canonizing fan labor.

plays.story: BlueNoroff's new Zoom-based phishing kit profiles victims' crypto wallets before delivering malware, blending social engineering with targeted crypto theft

angles.itsalreadypriced: Title: 'North Korea's BlueNoroff Is Casing Your Wallet Before the Zoom Call Even Starts' — frame as a market-risk story: state-sponsored actors are now doing reconnaissance on holdings before striking, raising the cost of careless self-custody habits ahead of any hack headlines.
angles.itsalreadywhen: Title: 'Recon-First Malware: Inside the Zoom Phishing Kit That Profiles You Before It Infects You' — the inevitability angle: this is the next evolution of targeted attacks — profiling precedes payload, meaning 'it's already when' the call started, not when the malware lands.

plays.story: SparkKitty malware hidden in mobile apps scans users' photo libraries specifically for crypto wallet seed phrases

angles.itsalreadypriced: Title: 'Your Screenshot of Your Seed Phrase Is Now a Liability: SparkKitty Hunts Wallets Photo by Photo' — a self-custody wake-up call tying directly into the same week's Triple-A and WEMIX hot-wallet losses: the common thread is basic opsec failures, not protocol bugs.
angles.itsalreadywhen: Title: 'SparkKitty Doesn't Wait for You to Get Phished — It Just Reads Your Photos' — the passive-surveillance angle: malware that mines existing data (camera rolls) rather than tricking you into an action marks a shift toward assume-breach mobile threat models.
